newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade council elects opposition mayor.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade council elects opposition mayor.

text.p: Serbia's opposition coalition, victorious in a three-month battle with ruling socialists for control of Belgrade's city council, elected Democratic Party leader Zoran Djindjic as mayor on Friday.

Djindjic, who was widely expected to win and was the only candidate, was elected with 68 votes to loud applause in the chamber. The Zajedno (Together) coalition holds 69 out of 110 seats in the assembly.
The three-party coalition forced the ruling socialists to recognise its gains in local elections last November by holding daily street protests, breaking their 50-year grip on power in the city.
President Slobodan Milosevic's socialists still control both the Serbian and Yugoslav governments.
The coalition faces an uphill struggle in Belgrade, inheriting power in a city that has little money to pay for badly needed reforms and modernisation.
There were 24 votes against Djindjic, two spoilt ballots and 17 abstentions. One delegate was not present.
